labels.label: prop:branched_covering_composition

hypotheses.paper: standing: X, Y, Z Hausdorff, LPC, first countable
hypotheses.note: (i)=>(ii): Y T2 LPC FC, Z T1 LPC FC, nothing on X; (ii)=>(i): X, Y, Z T2 LPC, Z FC

hypotheses.paper: (implicit at l.1137) a composite of coverings is a covering
hypotheses.note: added: q has finite fibres, OR Z1 = ord_q(Z) minus cl(q(Y minus ord_p(Y))) semilocally simply connected
the equivalence holds with the closure of q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) skeletal; the printed (ii) still implies (i)

findings: (i) => (ii) is FALSE as printed (l.1093, l.1129): the proof shows q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) is contained in Z minus ord_{q o p}(Z) (formalized in full, GX.preimage_ordY_comp_subset) and then concludes 'the latter is skeletal, thus so is the former', but a subset of a skeletal set is skeletal only if it is closed, and q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) need not be closed since q is not a closed map. Counterexample formalized: GX.not_isSkeletal_of_isBranchedCovering_comp (p the maximal covering of D_inf branched over {apex} and b_n = (1+e_n, n+e_n), e_n = 1/(|n|+2); q : D_inf -> D; q o p IS a branched covering, but q(branching locus) = {(1+e)exp(2 pi i e)} (plus possibly 0) accumulates at 1 and misses it, so it is not closed). The true statement: (i) <=> the CLOSURE of q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) is skeletal.

(ii) => (i), l.1137: '(q o p)|X1 -> Z1 is a composition of covering hence a covering' uses that a composite of coverings is a covering, which is false in general (GX.Topology.UniversalCover SCOPE 2). The proof is completed under either standard hypothesis: q of finite fibres (GX.isBranchedCovering_comp_of_finite) or Z1 semilocally simply connected (GX.isBranchedCovering_comp_of_semilocallySimplyConnected); GX.isBranchedCovering_comp_of_isCoveringMap isolates the step. Whether the statement fails without such a hypothesis is not formalized.

l.1116: 'An argumentation alike the one of Lemma lem:spread_partial_covering yields a contradiction' is replaced by a direct clopen argument (GX.subset_of_injOn_image_subset: two images p(U_i), p(U_j) meeting are equal, Y Hausdorff, q open and injective on each, U connected).
questions: Should the author change (ii) to 'the closure of q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) is skeletal' (equivalently 'q(Y minus ord_p(Y)) is contained in a skeletal set') and add 'q has finite fibres or Z semilocally simply connected in the strong sense' to the statement?

labels.label: rem:completion_covering

hypotheses.note: X T0 and Y T2, locally connected for the isomorphism with the space of ends; none for 'X is a completion of p^{-1}(U) -> Y'

questions: 'Isomorphic to the completion' read as: X is a completion (paper's sense) of p^{-1}(U) -> Y, the space of ends is one, and X is isomorphic to it (indeed to any T0 completion) by a unique homeomorphism over Y and under p^{-1}(U).

labels.label: prop:universality

hypotheses.paper: Y connected, locally path-connected, Hausdorff; S skeletal; Y minus S semilocally simply connected
Y first countable (section 3 standing assumption, l.810)
hypotheses.note: used for local path-connectedness of the Fox completion and lem:complete_path_carac

questions: 'Maximal among such branched coverings' read as GX.IsMaximalPossiblyBranched: dominates, by a branched covering over Y, every covering possibly branched over S (T2, LPC, first countable total space, in a fixed universe); uniqueness is proved for maximality tested in Y's universe, and in the stronger form GX.maxBranched_unique (any covering possibly branched over S with a continuous map over Y to the maximal one is isomorphic to it). The universal cover is based at a chosen y0 in Y minus S (exists: GX.nonempty_compl_of_isSkeletal).

labels.label: rem:one_could_sum_up

hypotheses.note: Y T2 LPC FC; total spaces T2 LPC

questions: The equivalence of categories is not formalized as a functor equivalence; formalized: the completion of a connected covering of a portly O is a branched covering possibly branched over the complement with preimage of O equal to the covering, every branched covering possibly branched over the complement of O restricts to a connected covering of O of which it is the completion, and covering morphisms extend to branched coverings between completions (functoriality and uniqueness of the extension are GXScaffold.Spread.Completion's IsFoxCompletion.existsUnique_extend).

labels.label: rem:considering_maximal_covering_possibly
questions: S^2 is the unit sphere of EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3); 'trivial' read as: the projection of the maximal covering is a homeomorphism; 'the branching locus is empty' proved, hence different from S.

labels.label: cex:proposition_prop_branched_covering

hypotheses.paper: S skeletal, Y minus S semilocally simply connected
hypotheses.note: false for the paper's S; S replaced by S union {apex}, which is skeletal with SLSC complement

findings: l.1184 'We see that S is skeletal' is FALSE: since (r_n, theta_n) is dense in Y0 = {theta in ]0,1[}, r_n takes arbitrarily small values, so the apex of D_inf is in the closure of S = (r_n, theta_n + n) but not in S; S is not closed, hence not skeletal (GX.cexS_not_isSkeletal), and prop:universality does not apply to it. 'Y minus S is semi-locally simply connected' also fails at the apex (every neighbourhood {r < eps} contains points of S around which a small loop is not null-homotopic) - not formalized. Correction: use S' = S union {apex}; then S' is skeletal, D_inf minus S' is semilocally simply connected, the maximal covering p possibly branched over S' is branched at every point of S (GX.logChart_mem_branchingLocus), q(S) is dense in D (GX.dense_qDisc_image_cexS), and q o p is not a branched covering (GX.cex_branched_covering_composition, via the corrected (i) => (ii)).

The disc D = Gamma_alpha \ D_inf is identified with C (GX.discHomeomorph); the 'theta_n + n' of the construction requires alpha = 1, which is taken (q(r, theta) = r exp(2 pi i theta)); q is proved a branched covering (GX.isBranchedCovering_qDisc), branched over {0} only.
questions: alpha is not specified at l.1183; alpha = 1 is the reading that makes q(r_n, theta_n + n) = q(r_n, theta_n).

kb_proposals: A composite of spreads is a spread (GX.IsSpread.comp); if q o Phi is a spread and q, Phi continuous then Phi is a spread (GX.IsSpread.of_comp) - this is how a morphism over Y between branched coverings is shown to be a spread.

To show a map G : X1 -> X2 over Y between branched coverings is a branched covering, use lem:complete_path_carac (iv) with X1' = p1^{-1}(O), Y1' = p2^{-1}(O): partial lifts extend by completeness of p1 and density of [0,1) (GX.isBranchedCovering_of_comm).

Branch points of a Fox completion of a universal covering are detected by a loop whose lift to the universal covering would close up inside an evenly covered component; non-triviality of the loop is then shown through Complex.isCoveringMap_exp and liftPath_apply_one_eq_of_homotopicRel (GX.logChart_mem_branchingLocus, GX.not_homotopic_refl_of_exp_lift).

DInfty is now LocPathConnectedSpace, FirstCountableTopology, PathConnectedSpace (radial paths, GX.DInfty.radialPath) and q = cplx 1 : DInfty -> C is a branched covering (GX.isBranchedCovering_qDisc); DInfty.logChart : C -> DInfty is an open embedding onto {r > 0} with q o logChart = exp.
notes: Single new file, 1887 lines, 0 sorry, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for all main theorems; lake build GXScaffold.Branched.Universality succeeded without rebuilding GX or mathlib. Imports GXScaffold.Branched.Basic, GX.Topology.UniversalCover and GXScaffold.Singular.Quotient (read-only). The two formal counterexamples (corrected cex; printed (i)=>(ii)) reuse prop:universality itself (maximal covering of D_inf branched over a discrete set plus the apex). No existing file edited.
